description: Where the hand model stands against published data, step by step. 'quantities' holds the literature values (with spread, source and protocol); 'steps' holds the model values recorded by scripts/hand_literature_comparison.py after each change of the hand. docs/wiki/hand-literature-comparison.md is generated from this file. Literature values are cited, never copied from figures: each row names the table it comes from.

mcfarland2023.citation: McFarland et al. A musculoskeletal model of the hand and wrist capable of simulating functional tasks. IEEE Trans Biomed Eng 70(5):1424-1435, 2023.
mcfarland2023.note: Protocols and results of its ARMS model are cited only; no ARMS file, parameter or coordinate is used.

odriscoll1992.citation: O'Driscoll SW et al. The relationship between wrist position, grasp size, and grip strength. J Hand Surg Am 17(1):169-177, 1992.

valerocuevas2003.citation: Valero-Cuevas FJ et al. Towards a realistic biomechanical model of the thumb: the choice of kinematic description may be more critical than the solution method or the variability/uncertainty of musculoskeletal parameters. J Biomech 36(7):1019-1030, 2003.

mathiowetz1985.citation: Mathiowetz V, Kashman N, Volland G, Weber K, Dowe M, Rogers S. Grip and pinch strength: normative data for adults. Arch Phys Med Rehabil 66:69-72, 1985.
mathiowetz1985.note: Right hand, all subjects (n = 628, ages 20-94); pounds converted at 4.448 N/lb. Table 2 (grip, Jamar second handle position), Table 3 (tip pinch), Table 4 (key pinch).

dallard2018.citation: Dallard J, Merlhiot X, Petitjean N, Duprey S. MRI-based experimentations of fingertip flat compression: geometrical measurements and finite element inverse simulations to investigate material property parameters. J Biomech 67:166-171, 2018.
dallard2018.note: Index fingertip, 5 men (32 +- 8 years), MRI. Table 2 (soft-tissue thickness normal to the pad at 0, 45 and 90 deg), Table 3 (deflection under flat compression).

misirlioglu2018.citation: Ozekli Misirlioglu T, Ozyemisci Taskiran O. Reliability of sonographic muscle thickness measurements of the thenar and hypothenar muscles. Muscle Nerve 57(1):E14-E17, 2018.
misirlioglu2018.note: Both hands of 15 volunteers, ultrasound. Table 2. Muscle thickness only: a lower bound for the soft tissue under the palm pads.

karademir2022.citation: Karademir F, Ayhan Kuru C, Arin G, Soylu R. Morphometry of thenar muscles by water bath ultrasonography in trapeziometacarpal osteoarthritis: intra- and inter-rater reliability. J Hand Surg Eur Vol, 2022.
karademir2022.note: Eight healthy volunteers (medians), Tables 2-3. Muscle thickness only: a lower bound.

leijnse2010.citation: Leijnse JNAL, Quesada PM, Spoor CW. Kinematic evaluation of the finger's interphalangeal joints coupling mechanism: variability, flexion-extension differences, triggers, locking swanneck deformities, anthropometric correlations. J Biomech 43(12):2381-2393, 2010.
leijnse2010.note: 17 hands of 9 healthy adults (33 +- 11 years); maximum passive flexion and extension per joint with a goniometer, digits 2-5 pooled per hand (Table 1).

steps.title: Step 1: hand models derived from the arm by generic pruning
steps.summary: No arm model changes (every MjModel array of myoarm_r, myoarms, myotorso_arms and myofullbody is identical before and after). myohand_r and myohands are the arm pruned; their actuators, tendons, equalities and pairs equal the arm's. This is the baseline of the rebuild, measured on myoarm_r.
notes: The grip is a fresh optimisation on this commit (balanced wrist, four restarts); its digit shares differ from the cached optimum in hand-function-validation.md (30 / 37 / 25 / 8 %) by up to 14 points.
No contact pair of myoarm_r involves a finger: in the active fist the fingers pass into the palm geoms and each other (negative fingertip-to-palm distances).

Fingertip values re-measured with the method of S1 (palmar direction from the long flexor, D_N0 at the distal palmar corner); the first recording measured along the old pads' normals, which point dorsally (see S1).

steps.title: S0: side suffix on every right-arm name
steps.summary: Names only. scripts/compare_model_numerics.py finds every MjModel array, and the tendon lengths, actuator lengths and moments, passive forces and body positions at five random postures, identical to step 1 in myohand_r, myohands, myoarm_r, myoarms, myotorso_arms, myofullbody and both hand fragments. The hand-function protocols rerun on the renamed model give the same numbers to the last printed digit, so the model stands where it stood after step 1.
notes: Fingertip values re-measured with the method of S1 (palmar direction from the long flexor, D_N0 at the distal palmar corner); the first recording measured along the old pads' normals, which point dorsally (see S1).

steps.title: S1: hand self-contacts and pads
steps.summary: Fingertip pads moved to the palmar side and fitted to Dallard's D_N0 (6.4 mm, scaled by distal-phalanx length); palm, thenar and hypothenar pads; 144 self-contact pairs per hand in one shared file used by every model with a hand. Before = S0 with the same validation scenes (the scenes now remove the model's own contact pairs, as the protocol states).
notes: Grip: the dynamometer is moved palmarly until it touches the palm, which is now the 19 mm palm pad instead of the metacarpal capsules; the dynamometer sits 11 mm further palmar, so the hand closes on it wider open. The self-selected grip falls below the in-vivo band (O'Driscoll 1992 mean - 1 SD = 270.7 N) and the digit shares move to within 4 points of the ARMS shares.

Active fist: digits 2, 4 and 5 touch the palm and hypothenar pads (within 0.8 mm); digit 3 stops 18 mm short, held by its neighbours (with MCP abduction free the flexing fingers converge). Penetration beyond each pair's margin stays below 1 mm.

The palm pad thickness (19.1 mm) comes from the fist criterion with the joints at their flexion limits; the model's PIP limit (90 deg) is below the usual 100-110 deg, so the fingertips land farther from the bones than in a real fist and the pad compensates.

Tenodesis and lateral pinch are unchanged: their scenes remove all model contact pairs (the protocol). With the self-contacts kept, tenodesis with MCP abduction locked fails the direction check (largest reversal 2.6 deg against 2 deg): fingers 2-4 converge and push each other.

steps.title: S1b: PIP flexion range from the literature
steps.summary: PIP flexion limit of digits 2-5 raised from 90 to 115 deg (Leijnse et al. 2010, maximum passive flexion, 115 +- 7 deg); palm pads refitted to the fist at the new limits; the PIP springs refitted (they change by less than 0.01 %); EDM loses a wrap that switched on abruptly near PIP5 108 deg. Before = S1.
notes: Grip: with the 8.0 mm palm pad (was 19.1 mm) the dynamometer sits closer to the metacarpals and the fingers close further around it. The self-selected grip rises from 232.5 to 310.3 N, back inside the in-vivo band (O'Driscoll 1992 mean - 1 SD = 270.7 N), and the settled grip from 132.8 to 282.9 N. The digit shares (29.5 / 38.0 / 22.9 / 9.5 %) are within 6 points of the ARMS shares.
Active fist: digits 2, 4 and 5 touch the palm and hypothenar pads; digit 3 still stops short, now 14.4 mm (was 18.5 mm), held by its neighbours.

Palm pad: 8.0 mm with the fingertips at the new flexion limits, close to the hypothenar muscle thickness of Misirlioglu (8.4 +- 1.9 mm); the hypothenar pad changes little (16.8 mm), as digit 5 lands on it with MCP and DIP, not PIP, setting the reach.
Tenodesis passes all checks; trial A ROM of digit 5 PIP is 80 deg, the other values move by at most 2 deg. Lateral pinch is unchanged (no thumb change).

Passive PIP moment near the new end range (muscles at act = 0 plus springs, other joints at 0): index -0.08 / -0.11 / -0.14 N m at 90 / 100 / 115 deg, digits 3-4 -0.07 to -0.10 N m; Kamper 2002 measured up to 60 deg (held at -0.04 N m beyond). The excess over the held value comes from the interosseous and lumbrical bundles stretched over the PIP (LU_RB, UI_UB), which a restoring spring cannot remove. Digit 5: -0.16 / -0.24 N m at 90 / 100 deg, but LU_RB5 turns into a PIP flexor at 114-115 deg (its wrap over Fifthpm_wrap_r switches side), so the total becomes +0.16 N m at the limit; the lumbrical paths are rebuilt in S5.
